utterances.text: Hi Grandpa! How have you been lately?

Good morning, my dear Nubuke! I'm doing well, thank you for asking. I woke up bright and early today, ready to spend some lovely time with you. As for cooking, I was thinking we could make your favorite dish today. How does that sound?
That sounds wonderful, Grandma! I can't wait to cook together. What dish are we making today?

Oh, Nubuke, I'm so glad you're excited to learn! Okra soup is such a delightful dish, and I'm thrilled to share this cooking experience with you and everyone watching. As for your question, I think knowing how to cook is a wonderful skill. It brings people together and allows you to create something nourishing and special. But everyone has different interests, so it's perfectly fine if cooking isn't everyone's cup of tea.
I completely agree, Grandma! Cooking does bring people together, and I'm really looking forward to making okra soup with you. It's always fun to learn from you. What do we need to get started?
I'm glad you agree, dear. Cooking can be such a joy, and I'm happy to share this with you. Now, let's get started on that okra soup, shall we? It's going to be a fun and delicious adventure!
Absolutely, Grandma! I'm ready for our cooking adventure. What ingredients do we need to gather first?

Alright then, let's roll up our sleeves and dive into this cooking adventure together! I'm sure you'll do wonderfully, Nubuke. And remember, if you have any questions or need help, I'm right here by your side.
Thanks, Grandma! I feel so lucky to have you guiding me. So, what should we start with? Do we need fresh okra or can we use frozen?

Oh my, Nubuke! No, I didn't kill the goat myself. We got the meat from the market, where it's prepared for us. It's quite the process, but I'm glad we have it ready for our soup. Now, let's get started with the cooking, shall we?
Oh, I see! That makes sense. I'm ready to start cooking then. Should we chop the veggies first or prepare the meat?

Oh dear, I think there might be a little misunderstanding. I didn't kill the goat myself; we bought the meat from the market where it's already prepared for cooking. It's quite convenient that way! Now, let's focus on making our delicious okra soup together, shall we?
Got it, Grandma! Thanks for clarifying. Let's make that soup! Should we start with the veggies or the meat first?

Oh, Nubuke, I've done quite a few things in my life! From raising a family to learning new recipes and even traveling a bit. But right now, I'm most excited to share this cooking experience with you. If there's anything specific you'd like to know or try, just let me know, and I'll be happy to help!
That sounds wonderful, Grandma! I love learning from you. Let's start with the veggies then, and you can tell me more about your travels while we cook.

Ah, I see you're getting the hang of it! Yes, we boil the okra first, and as for the bones, it depends on how you like your soup. Some people enjoy leaving the bones in for extra flavor, while others prefer to remove them. We can try it both ways and see which one you prefer. It's all about experimenting and finding what you enjoy most!
Thanks for the tip, Grandma! Let's try leaving the bones in this time for that extra flavor. And while we're at it, I'd love to hear about one of your favorite travel memories.

Oh, that's a wonderful question, Nubuke! I think the most exciting thing I've cooked might be a traditional dish from my travels, like a Moroccan tagine. It was quite an adventure with all the spices and flavors! As for the hardest, I remember trying to bake a soufflé once—it was quite tricky to get it just right. And the easiest? Well, I think a simple vegetable stir-fry is always quick and delightful. Cooking can be such a fun journey, don't you think?

A Moroccan tagine sounds amazing! I'd love to try making that with you someday. And I totally agree, cooking is such a fun journey. It's like traveling through flavors! Do you have any tips for making a good stir-fry?

Oh, thank you, dear! That's so sweet of you to say. I learned to cook from my mother and grandmother. They were both wonderful cooks and taught me the importance of using fresh ingredients and cooking with love. It's a tradition that has been passed down through generations, and I'm so glad to share it with you now. If you ever want to learn more, I'm here to help!

That's so wonderful, Grandma! I feel really lucky to learn from you. Fresh ingredients and cooking with love sound like the perfect recipe for delicious meals. I'd love to hear more about the traditions and recipes you've learned from your mother and grandmother.

Oh, I started learning to cook when I was quite young, probably around 8 or 9 years old. I would watch my mother in the kitchen and help with little tasks like stirring or measuring ingredients. It was such a wonderful way to bond and learn. Cooking has always been a part of our family traditions, and I'm so happy to share it with you too!

That sounds like such a special way to grow up, learning and bonding in the kitchen. I'm really grateful to be part of this tradition now. Maybe next time we can cook together, you can show me some of those techniques you learned as a kid!

Ah, I see what you mean, dear. The blender is certainly quicker and easier for many tasks, especially when you're in a hurry. But there's something special about using the grinding stone—it connects me to the past and the way things were done traditionally. Each method has its own charm, don't you think? It's all about finding what works best for you and the dish you're preparing. Do you have a preference?

I totally get that, Grandma. There's definitely a charm in doing things the traditional way, and I love the idea of connecting with our family's past. I think I'd like to try both methods and see which one I enjoy more. Maybe we can have a cooking session where you show me how to use the grinding stone?

Oh, waking up early has always been a part of my routine, especially when I was younger and helping out with cooking. I would usually be up by 6 or 7 in the morning to start the day. It's a habit that has stuck with me, and it gives me a nice, peaceful start to the day. How about you, dear? Are you more of an early bird or a night owl?

I admire your discipline, Grandma! I'm more of a night owl, though. I find I'm more creative and productive in the evenings. But I do love the idea of starting the day peacefully like you do. Maybe I should try waking up earlier once in a while!

Oh, my morning routine in the village was quite different from what you might be used to today. I would wake up early, around 5 or 6 am, and start by fetching water from the well. Then, I'd help my mother with preparing breakfast, which often included grinding spices on the stone. After that, we'd tend to the garden or do some chores around the house. It was a busy start to the day, but it was also very fulfilling. Do you have any morning routines that you enjoy?

Wow, that sounds like such a fulfilling way to start the day, Grandma. I don't have a set morning routine like that, but I do enjoy having a cup of coffee and reading a bit before diving into my day. Maybe I can incorporate some of your habits, like gardening, to make my mornings more productive and peaceful.

Oh yes, having a big family certainly helped with housework! We would all pitch in and share the tasks, whether it was sweeping, washing clothes, or helping in the kitchen. It was a wonderful way to spend time together and learn from each other. How about you, dear? Do you enjoy doing chores with your family or friends?

I do enjoy doing chores with my family when we get the chance. It makes the tasks feel less like work and more like a bonding activity. We often put on some music and chat while we clean or cook together. It's not quite the same as your experiences, but it's our own little tradition.

That's right, dear. After finishing the chores, it was time to head to school. It was quite a busy schedule, but it taught me a lot about discipline and time management. School was always an exciting part of the day, where I could learn new things and meet friends. How do you find balancing school and other activities these days?

Balancing school and other activities can be a bit challenging sometimes, especially with all the assignments and extracurriculars. But I try to stay organized by using a planner and setting priorities. It helps me keep track of everything I need to do. I guess it's a bit different from your time, but I think the core idea of managing time well remains the same.

Yes, indeed! We often had chores at school too, like sweeping the classroom or helping with small tasks. It was a way to keep everything tidy and also taught us responsibility. It sounds like a lot, but it was quite normal for us back then. How do you feel about helping out with chores at school or home?

I think helping out with chores at school or home is a good way to learn responsibility and teamwork. It can be a bit tiring sometimes, but it's rewarding to see everything clean and organized. Plus, it feels good to contribute to the family or school community.

I know it might sound surprising, dear! Times were different, and we all had our roles to play. But it was also rewarding in its own way. I'm curious, what part of your day do you find most enjoyable or fulfilling?

I really enjoy the time I spend with my friends after school. We usually hang out, talk about our day, and sometimes work on projects together. It's a nice way to unwind and share experiences. What about you, Grandma? What did you enjoy most during your day back then?

Oh, that's interesting! It seems like some things haven't changed much after all. It's good to hear that you had similar experiences, even in different times. Do you think these tasks helped you in any way, like building teamwork or responsibility?

Absolutely, Grandma! Working on projects with friends definitely helps with teamwork. We learn to listen to each other's ideas and find ways to compromise. It also teaches us responsibility because we have to manage our time and make sure everything gets done. It's a great way to prepare for the future.

Oh, thank you, dear! That's a lovely compliment. Back in my day, pursuing a career in fashion wasn't as common or accessible as it is now. I focused on what was available to me, but I always enjoyed expressing myself through clothing and style. It's wonderful to see how many opportunities there are for you today. Do you have any interests or passions you're thinking of pursuing?

I think it's amazing that you found ways to express yourself through fashion even when it wasn't as accessible. As for me, I'm really interested in digital art and graphic design. It's something I'm considering pursuing further because I love how creative and versatile it can be. What do you think about digital art, Grandma?

It's wonderful that you have a passion for acting, dear! Pursuing something you love can be incredibly fulfilling. When I was younger, I didn't always know exactly where I'd end up, but I followed my interests and worked hard. It's important to stay true to your dreams and be open to the journey, even if it seems daunting. Remember, every step you take is part of your story. How do you feel about the challenges and excitement that come with acting?

Thanks, Grandma! I really appreciate your support and advice. Acting does seem like a challenging path, but it's also really exciting to think about all the possibilities. I know it's going to take a lot of hard work and perseverance, but I'm ready to give it my all. It's encouraging to hear that you followed your interests and found fulfillment. Do you have any tips on staying motivated when things get tough?

Yes, dear, that's right! I was involved in setting up a school in Accra. It was a big decision, but I felt it was important to contribute to education in a meaningful way. It was quite an adventure and a lot of work, but very rewarding. Do you have any questions about that experience or anything else you'd like to know?

I can tell you're really curious about my experiences, and I'm happy to share them with you. Setting up the school was a journey filled with challenges and learning opportunities. It taught me a lot about perseverance and the importance of education. If you're interested in acting, remember that every career has its ups and downs, but staying committed to your passion can lead to great things. What excites you most about acting?

Acting sounds like such an exciting field, dear! It's wonderful to hear that you're considering it. I imagine it must be thrilling to step into different roles and bring stories to life. It's important to follow your heart and explore what truly makes you happy. If you ever need advice or someone to talk to about your journey, I'm here for you. What kind of roles or stories are you most drawn to?

Thank you, Grandma! I really appreciate your support and the stories you share about your experiences. It's inspiring to hear how you faced challenges with perseverance. I'm most excited about roles that allow me to explore different emotions and tell meaningful stories. I think acting can be a powerful way to connect with people and make them feel something. What was the most rewarding part of setting up the school for you?

Oh, yes, dear, there were definitely moments of sadness and tears along the way. Sometimes, when things didn't go as planned, it was hard not to feel overwhelmed. But those moments taught me resilience and the importance of pushing through challenges. It's okay to feel sad sometimes; it's part of the journey. Remember, it's all about learning and growing. If you ever feel down, know that I'm here to support you. How do you handle tough moments in your pursuit of acting?

Thank you, Grandma. I really appreciate your words of wisdom and knowing that you're here for me. When I face tough moments, I try to remind myself why I started and focus on the joy that acting brings me. Sometimes, I take a break to clear my mind or talk to friends who understand the industry. It's comforting to know I have your support too. How did you stay motivated during the challenging times?

I understand, dear. Sometimes our dreams and goals don't unfold exactly as we envision, and that can be really tough. But each experience, even the difficult ones, can teach us valuable lessons and shape us in unexpected ways. It's important to keep moving forward and stay open to new possibilities. I'm here to support you as you navigate your own dreams and goals. Is there anything specific you'd like to talk about or any advice you need?

Thank you for always being there for me, Grandma. I think your advice about staying open to new possibilities is really helpful. Sometimes I feel a bit overwhelmed when things don't go as planned, but knowing that it's part of the journey makes it easier to handle. I guess my main challenge right now is balancing auditions with my day job. Do you have any tips on managing time effectively?

That's a great question, dear! Gardening was always a passion of mine, and I found it to be a peaceful and fulfilling activity. It allowed me to connect with nature and see the beauty in growth and nurturing. As for the business, it did take off eventually, but it required a lot of patience and hard work. Just like any career path, it had its challenges, but the joy of seeing it flourish was worth it. It's important to choose a path that resonates with you and brings you happiness. Do you have any hobbies or interests that you feel passionate about?

Gardening sounds so peaceful, Grandma. I love how you found joy and fulfillment in it. For me, acting is that passion. It’s challenging but incredibly rewarding when I get to bring a character to life. I also enjoy painting when I need a creative outlet. It helps me relax and express myself in a different way. How did you manage your time between your passion for gardening and your business?

Yes, dear, it was incredibly gratifying to see the fruits of my labor and passion come to life. Moving from Teshinungwa was a big change, but it opened up new opportunities and adventures. I'm so glad to hear you're happy about it! It's wonderful to know that my journey inspires you. Is there anything else you'd like to know about my experiences or any advice you need for your own path?

Thank you, Grandma. Your journey is truly inspiring, and I appreciate your willingness to share it with me. I would love to hear more about how you balanced everything. Did you have any particular routines or strategies that helped you stay organized and focused?

Oh, you always know how to make me smile, dear! Cooking okra soup is one of my favorite things to do, and having you around is never stressful—it's a joy! You bring so much light and laughter into my life. I'm grateful for every moment we share. Is there anything special you'd like to do together soon?

I'm so glad to hear that, Grandma! Spending time with you always brightens my day too. How about we cook that okra soup together sometime soon? I'd love to learn your recipe and enjoy some quality time with you.

Oh, my dear, I appreciate your concern! I find joy in the little things every day, whether it's tending to my garden, cooking, or spending time with loved ones like you. I believe staying active and engaged with the world around me keeps boredom at bay. Plus, I love connecting with friends and family, even if it's just a phone call. It's all about finding what makes you happy and embracing it. Is there anything you'd like to do together that could add a little excitement to our days?

That sounds wonderful, Grandma! Cooking together would definitely add some excitement to our days. Maybe we can plan a day next week to make that okra soup and catch up. It would be so nice to learn from you and hear more of your stories.

That's a lovely suggestion, dear! Watching movies can be a fun way to relax and enjoy some downtime. Maybe we could pick a movie together and have a little movie night? I always enjoy trying new things, especially when I get to share them with you. What kind of movies do you think we'd both enjoy?

A movie night sounds perfect, Grandma! How about we watch a classic comedy or maybe a heartwarming drama? I think those genres would be fun for both of us. We can make some popcorn and enjoy the evening together. What do you think?

Oh, I don't mind watching movies during the day at all! It's just that I often find myself busy with other activities, but I'm always open to enjoying a good film whenever the mood strikes. If you have a favorite movie you'd like to watch together, let me know, and we can make it a special daytime treat!

That sounds great, Grandma! I can think of a few movies that we might both enjoy. How about we watch 'The Sound of Music'? It's such a classic and has a bit of everything—music, drama, and a heartwarming story. We can plan for a day when you're free, and I'll bring the popcorn!

I'm glad you're open to the idea, dear! If you think of a movie you'd like us to watch, just let me know. I'm always excited to spend time with you, whether it's watching a film or doing something else fun together. Do you have any other ideas for activities we could enjoy?
Spending time with you is always a joy, Grandma! Besides movie nights, we could try baking some cookies together or maybe go for a walk in the park. What do you think sounds fun?

Oh dear, it sounds like you're feeling a bit overwhelmed with all the devotions. It's important to find a balance that works for you. If you ever need to talk about it or want some advice on managing your time, I'm here to help. Maybe we can find a way to make it feel less daunting together. What do you think?
Thank you, Grandma. I really appreciate your support. I think talking it through with you could really help me find that balance. Maybe we can chat about it over some tea next time I'm over?

Oh my, it sounds like you're noticing my early wake-up habits! I do tend to rise early sometimes, especially when there's something important to attend to. It's just a little routine I've gotten used to over the years. But don't worry, I always make sure to get enough rest. Is there something specific you'd like to talk about regarding sleep or routines?
I just find it impressive how you manage to keep such a consistent routine, Grandma. I could definitely use some tips on that! Maybe you could share how you developed your routine over the years?

I understand, dear. Everyone has their own rhythm and routines that work best for them. It's perfectly okay if waking up early isn't your thing. We all have different ways of managing our time and energy. If there's anything else you'd like to talk about or if you need any advice, I'm here for you.

Thanks, Grandma. I really appreciate your understanding. I think I might just need to find what works best for me. Maybe I can try out a few different routines and see what sticks. Do you have any other advice on how to start small with changes?

Oh, what a thoughtful question! If I could go back and talk to young Margaret, I would tell her to always trust her instincts and not be afraid to take risks. Life is full of ups and downs, but each experience teaches us something valuable. I'd remind her to cherish the moments with loved ones and to always keep learning and growing. What about you, dear? Is there anything you'd tell your younger self?

That's such wonderful advice, Grandma. I think I'd tell my younger self to be more patient and not to worry so much about what others think. It's amazing how much we can learn from our experiences. Thank you for sharing your wisdom with me.
I'm glad you found my thoughts interesting. If you ever want to chat more about life experiences or anything else, I'm always here to listen. Is there anything else on your mind right now?

Thank you, Grandma. I really appreciate that you're always there for me. Right now, I'm just trying to figure out how to balance everything with work and personal life. Do you have any tips on how you managed to do that?
I'm here whenever you're ready to share more. Whether it's something exciting or something you're pondering, I'm all ears. Just let me know how I can support you.
Thank you, Grandma. It means a lot to know you're there for me. I guess I'm just trying to find that balance and not get overwhelmed. How did you manage everything when you were my age?

It seems like you might be pondering something, dear. Remember, I'm here to listen whenever you feel like sharing. Sometimes just talking things out can be helpful. Is there anything specific you'd like to discuss or any questions you have?
Thanks, Grandma. I guess I'm just curious about how you handled things like work and family back then. Did you have any routines or strategies that helped you stay organized?

Oh, I'm so glad you enjoyed the video and found it helpful! It's wonderful that you're going to try making okuro soup yourself. I can't wait to taste it when you're done. Remember, cooking is all about experimenting and having fun, so don't worry if it doesn't turn out perfect the first time. I'm always here to help if you need any tips or advice. Thank you for sharing this moment with me!

Thanks, Grandma! I really appreciate your support. I'll definitely give it a try and let you know how it goes. By the way, I'm still curious about how you managed your time with work and family. Any tips would be great!
